sections.html:
Hobart is a Lake County city about 31 miles southeast of Chicago, on Deep River beside Lake George. The 2020 count was 29,752 residents and 12,709 housing units, with 5.6% of units vacant. The median owner-occupied home value is $215,200, and 69.5% of homes are owner-occupied. Those are citywide figures, so your own house may sit well above or below them.

Hobart has long been mostly residential, with a retail corridor added by annexation near Interstate 65 and U.S. Route 30, anchored by Southlake Mall. Three railroads run through the city: Norfolk Southern, Chicago, Fort Wayne and Eastern, and Canadian National. Train noise can affect homes near the tracks, and buyers sometimes ask about it, so be ready to answer honestly.

Hobart was platted in 1849, became a town in 1889 and was reincorporated as a city in 1921. Several downtown buildings are on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Hobart Carnegie Library, the Pennsylvania Railroad Station, the Hobart Commercial District and the First Unitarian Church of Hobart.

A city with that history has a mix of older houses and later additions. A house's age often decides how much updating a buyer expects, and homes near the lake, the trails or downtown tend to draw the first questions, so describe their location accurately.

sections.h2: Flood history and what to gather
sections.html:
Hobart has a documented flood history. The September 2008 flood in northwestern Indiana hit eleven communities especially hard, Hobart among them. That storm dropped between 2 and more than 11 inches of rain over September 12 to 15, 2008, causing two deaths and evacuations of hundreds of residents, and six northwestern Indiana counties were declared federal disaster areas.

If your house is near Deep River, Lake George or a creek, collect these before selling:

  • Any flood insurance policy and claim history.
  • Repair receipts for sump pumps, drainage and basement work.
  • A FEMA flood map check for the parcel.
  • Photos of the basement after heavy rain, if you have them.

Listing known water problems on the Indiana seller disclosure keeps a sale clean, and cash buyers usually price the risk in rather than walk away.

sections.h2: Fix it first or sell as-is?
sections.html: Before deciding, walk the house the way a buyer's inspector would. Note the wiring, plumbing, roof, basement and anything near the tracks that a buyer might ask about. Price out the fixes and add the weeks they take. A financed buyer will usually ask for repairs or a lower price, while a cash buyer builds the cost into the offer and closes without that back-and-forth. If repairs would use up most of what they add to the price, selling as-is can leave you with about the same money and far less work.

Most of Hobart is in the School City of Hobart. Some parts fall in the River Forest Community School Corporation or the Merrillville Community School District. Buyers with children often check which district a street belongs to, so confirm your address with the district before you describe the house.

The Building Department's email is building@cityofhobart.org. The Recorder is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The Building Department issues permits and inspects new construction and remodeling inside city limits. A permit is required before work starts, and the department also licenses contractors and handles building-related code complaints.

Chapter 115 of the municipal code requires rental owners to register each year with the Building Department by July 15. Registration needs proof of insurance, or a bond or letter of credit of at least $25,000. A property acquired after July 15 must be registered within 30 days of purchase, and a sale, transfer or end of rental use must be reported within 30 days.

Failing to register can bring a fine of up to $2,500 per unit per day, and repeat violations can reach $7,500 per unit per day. Selling a rented house? Make sure the registration is current and tell the buyer what rules come with the property.

sections.h2: Closing and recording in Lake County
sections.html:
After a sale, the Lake County Recorder in Crown Point files the deed. That office takes deeds, mortgages, liens, releases and leases, but generally not court orders, decrees, judgments or wills. If you are selling an inherited house, the right probate paperwork usually has to be sorted out before anyone can prepare a deed.

Both sides of an Indiana transfer fill out a sales disclosure form. It is reviewed by the county assessor, then filed by the county auditor ahead of the conveyance document. You will not usually chase these steps yourself, since the title company coordinates them.

Hobart property tax arrives as two installments, due May 10 and November 10. The installment nearest your sale date is normally prorated by the closing agent, and the title company pays any tax owed out of your proceeds. For today's balance, call the Lake County Treasurer.

Hobart sellers tend to be selling because of a life event or the condition of the house, and each one changes the timeline.

  • An older house near downtown with outdated wiring or plumbing.
  • Water in the basement after heavy rain.
  • A rental that needs registration or tenant turnover.
  • An inherited home split among several family members.
  • A move out of the Chicago commuter area on short notice.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
1. Send us the address and basics: condition, occupancy and any loan balance.
  2. We view the house and present an offer.
  3. On acceptance, the title company opens the file and searches for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You sign the sales disclosure form and the deed.
  5. The deed is recorded in Crown Point and you receive your proceeds.

Title issues cause most delays: an old lien, a name on the deed that was never updated or probate papers still outstanding. Mention any of these on the first call so the title company has time to work on them.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
We buy Hobart houses as-is. Describe the property, mention any water history or tenants, and we make an offer based on condition and location. Accept, and a title company searches the deed, prepares the disclosure form and sets a closing date. Repairs, cleanouts and showings drop off your list, and you are paid at closing.

Put any offer, cash or otherwise, in writing before committing. Disclose what you know, keep your repair records and ask for the closing date in writing.

An empty house still costs money each month, with utilities, insurance, lawn care and property tax all continuing, and a vacant property can suffer pipe damage in winter. Relatives who live elsewhere often prefer an as-is sale to repeated trips. Gather the estate papers, the tax bill and the keys, and ask the title company what the deed needs before closing.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental property in Hobart?
faqs.a: Yes. Hobart's municipal code requires annual rental registration with the Building Department by July 15, with proof of insurance or a bond or letter of credit of at least $25,000.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Hobart house?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded with the Lake County Recorder at 2293 N. Main Street, Building A, 2nd Floor, Crown Point. The phone number is 219-755-3730.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Hobart house in?
faqs.a: Most of Hobart is in the School City of Hobart, but some areas are in River Forest Community School Corporation or Merrillville Community School District. Check your address with the district.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hobart house with water damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Disclose what you know, keep repair records, and compare written offers. A cash buyer can purchase a house with damage as is.
